api/Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Aggregates.Ag.title: Enum AggregateFaultOrigin | Devbone Event-Driven Platform
api/Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Aggregates.Ag.summary: Enum AggregateFaultOrigin Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Aggregates Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.dll Identifies the lifecycle operation that made an aggregate instance unsafe for further domain use. The origin distinguishes deterministic replay failures from live command or event-tracking failures in diagnostics. public enum AggregateFaultOrigin Fields CommandHandling = 3 Indicates that a command handler raised an unexpected exception and may have left in-memory state uncertain. EventApplication = 0 Indicates that an event handler failed while applying a newly emitted event to live aggregate state. EventTracking = 1 Indicates that metadata creation or uncommitted-event tracking failed after an event was applied. Rehydration = 2 Indicates that a persisted stream could not be deserialized, validated structurally, or replayed.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Catalog.Event.summary: Class EventContractCatalogVerifier Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Catalog Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.dll Compares a catalogue against a published baseline and reports incompatible changes. public static class EventContractCatalogVerifier Inheritance object EventContractCatalogVerifier Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Enforces the event-evolution rules mechanically: additive optional properties and new contracts pass, renames, removals and type changes fail. The escape hatch for anything on the forbidden list is a new contract, never an edit to an existing one, because historic events keep their stored payload forever and must still deserialize into the current CLR type. The rules are deliberately not scoped by event version. Reading a stored event overwrites the payload's version field with the persisted one, so bumping a version neither breaks nor legitimizes anything — a changed version is reported as a signal, not as permission. api/Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Repositories..summary: Interface IAggregateLockPort Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Repositories Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.dll Coordinates exclusive aggregate ownership and returns a disposable lease to the successful caller. public interface IAggregateLockPort Remarks This is the application-facing DDD port. It is strongly typed over the aggregate identity, applies a bounded retry policy, and is what CommandExecutor depends on. An application implements or registers it; it does not talk to a database itself. Do not confuse it with Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Locks.IAggregateLockStore, which is the PostgreSQL advisory-lock store on the persistence side: untyped, no retry policy, and one layer below this port. An adapter implements this interface over that store. The Port suffix names that layer difference, which the former name ILockRepository left to the documentation. Methods TryLock<TIdentity>(IAggregateName, IRequestId, TIdentity, AggregateLockOptions?, CancellationToken) Attempts to acquire one globally identified aggregate lock according to a bounded retry policy. Returns Task<ILockResult> A result containing the owning disposable lock on success. Type Parameters TIdentity Strongly typed aggregate identity.

Returns Task<AggregateScenario<TAggregate, TEntity, TIdentity>> The same scenario so assertions can be chained. Remarks A failing command leaves nothing to commit, so the commit is skipped and CommitResult stays unchanged. That keeps a negative scenario readable: assert on Result and on an empty NewEvents().

api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Outbox.D.summary: Class OutboxDispatcherServiceCollectionExtensions Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Outbox.DependencyInjection Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Outbox.dll Registers the durable outbox dispatcher that claims persisted outbox rows and publishes them. public static class OutboxDispatcherServiceCollectionExtensions Inheritance object OutboxDispatcherServiceCollectionExtensions Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Methods AddDevboneEventResend(IServiceCollection, ResendOptions) Registers the operator-requested outbox replay executor. public static IServiceCollection AddDevboneEventResend(this IServiceCollection services, ResendOptions options) Parameters services IServiceCollection The service collection. options ResendOptions Replay execution settings. Returns IServiceCollection The same service collection so calls can be chained. Remarks Requires AddDevboneEventStore and AddDevboneEventBus. Every instance may host this: the request row's claim decides which one executes a given request, so no leader election or singleton deployment is needed. A replay reaches every consumer of the affected streams, including applications that do not belong to the requester. On a shared broker, confirm that foreign consumers are idempotent before enabling it. Exceptions ArgumentNullException Thrown when an argument is null. AddDevboneOutboxDispatcher(IServiceCollection, OutboxDispatcherOptions) Registers the outbox dispatcher and, in embedded mode, the hosted service that runs it. public static IServiceCollection AddDevboneOutboxDispatcher(this IServiceCollection services, OutboxDispatcherOptions options) Parameters services IServiceCollection The service collection. options OutboxDispatcherOptions Dispatcher settings including the owning event-store id and worker id. Returns IServiceCollection The same service collection so calls can be chained. Remarks Requires AddDevboneEventStore (for IOutboxStore and IOutboxNotificationListener) and AddDevboneEventBus (for IEventBusResolver). Publication is deliberately separate from persistence: a commit is durable once the event and its outbox row are written, and delivery is a later, independently retried step. Delivery is at-least-once. The dispatcher claims a row with a lease, publishes, then settles; a crash between publish and settle re-delivers after the lease expires, which is why consumers must settle manually and deduplicate. Exceptions ArgumentNullException Thrown when an argument is null.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Outbox.R.summary: Class ResendHostedService Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Outbox.Resend Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Outbox.dll Polls for operator-requested outbox replays and executes one at a time. public sealed class ResendHostedService : BackgroundService, IHostedService, IDisposable Inheritance object BackgroundService ResendHostedService Implements IHostedService IDisposable Inherited Members BackgroundService.StartAsync(CancellationToken) BackgroundService.StopAsync(CancellationToken) BackgroundService.Dispose() BackgroundService.ExecuteTask object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Every application instance may run this. api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Outbox.R.summary: Class ResendProcessor Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Outbox.Resend Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Outbox.dll Executes one claimed resend request by republishing already published outbox envelopes. public sealed class ResendProcessor Inheritance object ResendProcessor Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The envelope bytes are republished verbatim, exactly as they were first delivered. That is the property the whole feature rests on: a projection compares an incoming event with the one it already stored, and a byte-identical event is a no-op. Rebuilding the envelope instead — a fresh timestamp, a new trace context — would make every replayed event look like an identifier reused with different content, which dead-letters rather than repairs. Progress is reported against the claim. If the lease was taken over, the run stops immediately instead of racing the instance that now owns the request. It does not guarantee equality: delivery is at-least-once and later events may already have been merged, so Merged.EventSequence can be greater. Treat the document as current state, never as the state immediately after one specific event, and keep handlers idempotent. api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.D.summary: Class ProjectionServiceCollectionExtensions Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.DependencyInjection Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.dll Registers the projection pipeline: the always-on raw and merged layers, the transport adapters, and the derived layer that carries application-owned query models. public static class ProjectionServiceCollectionExtensions Inheritance object ProjectionServiceCollectionExtensions Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Methods AddDevboneEventProjection(IServiceCollection, IConfiguration, string) Registers the complete projection pipeline with options bound from configuration. public static IServiceCollection AddDevboneEventProjection(this IServiceCollection services, IConfiguration configuration, string sectionName = "EventProjection") Parameters services IServiceCollection The service collection. configuration IConfiguration Configuration containing the projection section. sectionName string The configuration section name. Defaults to SECTION_NAME. Returns IServiceCollection The same service collection so calls can be chained. Remarks Register application query models with AddProjectionHandler<THandler>(IServiceCollection) after calling this method. Every registration here is a singleton: the pipeline holds broker connections and a MongoDB client for the lifetime of the host, and no part of it is request-scoped. AddProjectionHandler<THandler>(IServiceCollection) Registers one application-owned derived projection handler. public static IServiceCollection AddProjectionHandler<THandler>(this IServiceCollection services) where THandler : class, IProjectionHandler Parameters services IServiceCollection The service collection. Returns IServiceCollection The same service collection so calls can be chained. Type Parameters THandler The handler implementation. Remarks Handlers observe merged state at least as new as the event they are handling, and inherit ordering, dedupe, bounded retry, and dead-lettering from the pipeline. Because delivery is at-least-once and the merged document may already reflect later events, handlers must be idempotent.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.M.title: Class ProjectionCompatibilityOptions | Devbone Event-Driven Platform
api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.M.summary: Class ProjectionCompatibilityOptions Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.MongoDb.Configuration Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.MongoDb.dll Configures fail-fast limits shared by event producers and MongoDB projection consumers. public sealed class ProjectionCompatibilityOptions Inheritance object ProjectionCompatibilityOptions Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Constructors ProjectionCompatibilityOptions() public ProjectionCompatibilityOptions() Fields DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_AGGREGATE_STATE_BYTES Default maximum BSON size of the final aggregate state validated at commit. public const int DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_AGGREGATE_STATE_BYTES = 1048576 Field Value int DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_DOCUMENT_DEPTH Default maximum supported JSON and BSON nesting depth. public const int DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_DOCUMENT_DEPTH = 64 Field Value int DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_EVENT_PAYLOAD_BYTES Default maximum UTF-8 or BSON size of one event payload. public const int DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_EVENT_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 262144 Field Value int DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_INTERMEDIATE_STATE_BYTES Default conservative upper bound for intermediate states in a multi-event commit. public const int DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_INTERMEDIATE_STATE_BYTES = 12582912 Field Value int Properties IsEnabled Gets or sets whether the write-side commit guard runs. Enabled by default. public bool IsEnabled { get; init; } Property Value bool Remarks Turning this off is the supported escape hatch for an application that provably does not project to MongoDB. It disables ValidateCommit(string, IReadOnlyCollection<string>) only, so aggregate commits stop being checked against BSON representability and MongoDB size limits. It deliberately does not disable the read-side checks in the projection pipeline: those guard an actual MongoDB write, where the limits are physical rather than a policy. Disabling it in a system that does project to MongoDB moves the failure from a recoverable command error to a permanently dead-lettered projection message and a read model that silently diverges. There is no supported repair for that, because the offending event is already immutable. MaximumAggregateStateBytes Gets or sets the maximum BSON size of the final aggregate state. public int MaximumAggregateStateBytes { get; init; } Property Value int MaximumDocumentDepth Gets or sets the maximum supported object and array nesting depth. public int MaximumDocumentDepth { get; init; } Property Value int MaximumEventPayloadBytes Gets or sets the maximum UTF-8 and BSON size of one event payload. public int MaximumEventPayloadBytes { get; init; } Property Value int MaximumIntermediateStateBytes Gets or sets the conservative maximum for the previous projection plus every patch in one commit. This protects event-by-event read processing without reproducing the projection on the write side. public int MaximumIntermediateStateBytes { get; init; } Property Value int Methods Validate() Validates configured limits before they are used for a commit. public void Validate() Exceptions InvalidOperationException Thrown when a limit is non-positive or internally inconsistent.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.P.title: Interface IRawProjectionStallReader | Devbone Event-Driven Platform
api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.P.summary: Interface IRawProjectionStallReader Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Persistence Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.dll Reads how far the raw layer is behind because an event of a stream never arrived. public interface IRawProjectionStallReader Remarks A separate port rather than another member on IRawProjectionStore: the ingestion port is implemented by consumers who replace the store, and widening it would break every one of them for a purely diagnostic capability. A missing event does not corrupt a read model — the contiguity gate stores later events without applying them, so the aggregate stalls instead of diverging. That is the better failure mode, but only if someone notices; otherwise "stalls instead of diverging" degrades into "diverges silently, one aggregate at a time". Methods GetStallSnapshotAsync(string, int, CancellationToken) Summarizes the events that are stored but not applied because an earlier event of their stream is missing. Task<RawProjectionStallSnapshot> GetStallSnapshotAsync(string aggregateName, int sampleLimit, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters aggregateName string Aggregate name. sampleLimit int Maximum number of aggregate identifiers to name in the sample. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancellation token. Returns Task<RawProjectionStallSnapshot> The current stall snapshot for this aggregate. Remarks Storing and applying happen in one transaction, so an event that is externally visible as unapplied is genuinely waiting for a predecessor rather than merely in flight.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.P.summary: Interface IProjectionHandler Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Projections Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.dll Builds one application-owned query model on top of the framework-standard raw and merged layers. public interface IProjectionHandler Remarks The raw and merged layers are configuration-only and identical for every application. A derived handler is where code belongs: traversals, aggregations, denormalizations and anything a configured reference join cannot express. Handlers run in their own consumer stage, so a failing handler dead-letters its own message and never blocks the merged layer. A handler that throws is retried by the transport; a handler that keeps throwing ends in the aggregate's dead-letter destination. Methods CanHandle(string) Determines whether this handler reacts to updates of one aggregate type. bool CanHandle(string aggregateName) Parameters aggregateName string Exact aggregate contract name. Returns Task A task completing after the query model has been updated durably. Remarks Must be idempotent: the same update can be delivered more than once, and the merged document may already reflect events after the announced sequence.

MissingReferencesRetryProcessor Retries incomplete same-tenant reference enrichment with bounded attempts. ProjectionDependency Identifies one direct aggregate dependency of a raw projection. ProjectionDependencyExtractor Extracts the direct aggregate dependencies represented by canonical IDs in a raw projection. ProjectionEnricher Replaces recognized aggregate IDs with same-tenant raw projection documents. ProjectionEnrichmentResult Contains an enriched projection and unresolved references. ProjectionReference Identifies one aggregate reference found in a JSON projection field. ProjectionStateTransition Applies lifecycle-aware event semantics to one raw aggregate projection. Interfaces IProjectionHandler Builds one application-owned query model on top of the framework-standard raw and merged layers. IProjectionReferenceResolver Resolves whether a JSON string field represents an aggregate reference. IProjectionReferenceSource Loads raw projection states used for cross-aggregate enrichment.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.W.summary: Class ProjectionStallDetector Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.Workers Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.dll Samples the stored-but-unapplied events of every configured aggregate and reports them as metrics and, past a configured age, as a warning. public sealed class ProjectionStallDetector : BackgroundService, IHostedService, IDisposable Inheritance object BackgroundService ProjectionStallDetector Implements IHostedService IDisposable Inherited Members BackgroundService.StartAsync(CancellationToken) BackgroundService.StopAsync(CancellationToken) BackgroundService.Dispose() BackgroundService.ExecuteTask object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The pipeline applies raw events only in contiguous sequence, so a missing event leaves later ones stored and unapplied: the aggregate stalls rather than diverging. That is the better failure mode and it is the reason a global read cursor was judged unnecessary — but it only holds while someone notices the stall. Nothing else in the pipeline does: the raw processor settles the message and adds zero to the applied counter, and the pending-notification sweep only looks at events that were already applied. Detection is separate from repair on purpose. Repair is an operator-triggered replay through the outbox, which reaches every consumer of the affected streams; this worker never triggers one, it only makes the need visible. api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Ddd.summary: Class AggregateRoutingCatalogExtensions Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Ddd.Catalog Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Ddd.dll Contributes configured routes to the event contract catalogue. public static class AggregateRoutingCatalogExtensions Inheritance object AggregateRoutingCatalogExtensions Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Contract names come from code; stream names do not. They are configuration, which is exactly where two applications sharing a broker collide hardest — one can silently publish into the other's topic. A catalogue built from the assembly alone would document the half of the namespace that is already the safest. Every retained route version is contributed, not only the current one, because events persisted under an earlier version keep pointing at it. Disabled when null or empty, which is the default. public string? StreamNamingConvention { get; init; } Property Value string Remarks On a broker shared by several applications, stream names are a cross-application namespace that nothing otherwise reserves or validates. Two applications can silently choose the same stream; each then publishes into the other's topic and consumes events it cannot interpret. A convention such as ^myapp\.[a-z0-9-]+\.events$ makes that collision impossible to configure by accident. The framework enforces the pattern, not the pattern's content: choosing and reserving the namespace is a platform-operations responsibility. Default off so an existing deployment is unaffected until it opts in. Remarks Takes plain identifier sets rather than the bus options type on purpose: routing is persisted with the event and consumed by the write side, so it must not depend on a transport package. A caller holding EventBusTargetsOptions passes options.Targets.Keys.ToHashSet(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase) after validating those options itself.

api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Dep.summary: Class EventStoreServiceCollectionExtensions Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.DependencyInjection Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.dll Registers the PostgreSQL event store with the lifetimes it requires. public static class EventStoreServiceCollectionExtensions Inheritance object EventStoreServiceCollectionExtensions Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The event store is a singleton. It owns a connection factory and validated settings, and holds no per-request state. Registering it as scoped or transient multiplies Npgsql connection factories per request — a mistake that does not fail, it only degrades, which is why this registration exists. Registering the store opens no connection. Network resources are opened only by explicit operations. api/Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Res.summary: Class ResendRequest Namespace Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Resend Assembly Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.dll Describes one operator-requested replay of already published outbox envelopes. public sealed class ResendRequest Inheritance object ResendRequest Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks A resend republishes the exact bytes persisted in the outbox, never a reconstructed envelope. That is what makes it safe: a projection recognizes a byte-identical event by its identifier and skips it, so replaying events a read model already has is a no-op rather than a corruption. [Range(1, 500)] public int DefaultPageSize { get; set; } Property Value int EnableResendRequests Gets or sets whether operators may request an outbox replay from the diagnostics UI. Disabled by default. public bool EnableResendRequests { get; set; } Property Value bool Remarks Even when enabled the Time Machine only records a request; it never publishes. Execution belongs to the application instances hosting the resend worker, which are the only processes with broker credentials. That separation is why a diagnostics UI embedded in an application can offer this at all. A replay reaches every consumer of the affected streams, including other applications on a shared broker. Enabling this therefore requires ResendAuthorizationPolicy; configuration validation rejects the combination of an enabled feature and an unset policy at startup. index.html.summary: Devbone Event-Driven Platform — API reference Generated from the XML documentation of the published packages. Every public type is here because missing documentation is a build error in this platform, not a warning. This reference answers what a type is and how it behaves. It does not explain how to stand an application up — that is the narrative guide, which lives with the source. Packages Package Purpose Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd Domain model, aggregates, commands, event contracts, privacy contracts, snapshot-facing ports. Devbone.Frameworks.Ddd.Testing In-memory persistence ports and a Given/When/Then aggregate harness. Development dependency. Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing PostgreSQL event store, optimistic concurrency, privacy index, snapshots, transactional outbox. Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.Ddd Direct-mode adapter over the event store, aggregate routing, stored-event mappers. Devbone.Frameworks.EventSourcing.TimeMachine Read-only diagnostics UI as a Razor class library. Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Contracts Broker-independent canonical envelope, metadata, lifecycle, privacy, headers. Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus Transport-neutral publish/subscribe, Kafka, RabbitMQ, manual settlement. Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Ddd Publication adapter turning stored events into canonical envelopes. Devbone.Frameworks.EventBus.Outbox Claim, publish, retry and settle dispatcher over the outbox port. Devbone.Frameworks.EventPersistence.Contracts Transport-neutral gateway wire contracts. Devbone.Frameworks.EventPersistence.Client Optional persistence-port adapter over HTTPS. Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection Kafka/RabbitMQ-to-MongoDB read pipeline: raw, merged and derived layers. Devbone.Frameworks.EventProjection.MongoDb Shared JSON/BSON conversion, compatibility and size limits. The deployable hosts — the projection worker, the persistence gateway and the standalone Time Machine host — are services rather than libraries and are deliberately absent. Versions See versions for the exact package versions this reference was generated from.
